title.narrative: Emowering the psychosocial assistants/APS in South Kivu

description.narrative: In post conflict situation, it is important to reconstruct communities. Among the main activities of reconstructions, the psychosocial care is very important as it helps people to manage their traumatic stories in order to reconstruct stakeholders’ lives. It is in this perspective that this project is elaborated to reduce people’s trauma. The project aims at reinforcing the capacity of the Psycho Social Assistants (otherwise known as APS) working in the trauma Centres that are managed by the Bukavu Justice and Peace Commission so that they can provide psychological assistance and support to the survivors of rape and sexual violence victims. The psychosocial assistance will concern the communities and individuals in need to be healed from trauma and thus enable them to restart a new life after conflict. The training will focus on individual and group counselling. Listening to traumatic stories can be very stressful and in most cases support agents can be as well affected and be traumatised in return. If the APS is not able to manage his own stress, he cannot provide significant assistance to other victims. This project is in perspective so as to help the APS keep the balance while listening and offering support to survivors and the traumatised subjects. The APS will also learn technical process to manage their own stress in order to be fit and strong to be in position to help others.
